title: Viewing the OS End of Life Dashboard

blocks.text: The OS End of Life dashboard provides visibility into assets running operating systems that have reached or are approaching End-of-Life (EOL) or End-of-Support (EOS) status. The dashboard includes summary tiles, charts, and tables that provides details of the EOL and EOS status of OS assets.

blocks.item: Mitigate security risks in unpatched and unsupported operating systems.
Strengthen regulatory and internal compliance posture.
Minimize operational disruptions due to outdated OS versions.

blocks.text: To create an OS EOL dashboard from a preconfigured template, go to Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > OS End of Life. To learn more, see Using Dashboard Templates.
The tiles display the total number of assets, including those that are reaching the EOL or EOS date, and the ones that have already reached the EOL or EOS date.

blocks.item: Total Active Assets in EOL

The number of active OS assets past their EOL date, which no longer receive security patches or updates. It directly measures the organization's security risk by revealing the total count of vulnerable OS assets. Click the asset number to view the list of active OS assets in EOL.
See image.
Assets Reaching EOL in the Next 6 Months

The number of OS assets reaching EOL in the next 6 months. This helps in proactive budgeting, migration, or replacement before an asset becomes a security liability. Click the asset number to view the list of OS assets.
Total Active Assets in EOS
The number of active OS assets past their EOS date. This data helps with effective security and risk management. Click the asset number to view the list of OS assets at EOS.
Assets Reaching EOS in the Next 6 Months

The number of OS assets reaching EOS in the next 6 months. The 6-month window provides necessary visibility for long-term planning, budgeting, or scheduling maintenance cycles well in advance. Click the asset number to view list of OS assets approaching EOS status in the next 6 months.

blocks.text: The charts and tables provide a detailed breakdown of key metrics categorized by EOL and EOS status.

blocks.item: Assets in EOL Overtime

The chart shows the historical trend of OS assets that are no longer supported by their vendors. This is critical for tracking the organization's performance in managing and reducing high-risk EOL assets. A consistent downward trend indicates successful remediation efforts. Conversely, a stable or upward trend signals that remediation is not keeping pace with assets reaching EOL, allowing you to identify and address issues. The chart's default view displays data from the last three months.
See image.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of active OS assets at EOL for that date.
See image.
Assets in EOS Overtime

The chart shows the historical trend of active OS assets in EOS. It helps track the growth of unsupported assets to prioritize upgrades. A rising trend indicates growing technical debt and security exposure, as these assets are not receiving essential security updates. Monitoring this trend is crucial for maintaining a secure and reliable IT environment. The chart's default view displays data from the last three months.
See image.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of active OS assets at EOS for that date.
See image.
OS EOL - Breakdown by Asset OS - Top 10
This chart lists the top 10 operating systems with the highest number of assets affected by EOL. It helps track OS assets using two metrics:
Active Assets in EOL: The dark blue bar represents assets currently in EOL, highlighting security risks and compliance gaps that require urgent attention.
Active Assets with OS EOL in 6 Months: The light blue bar represents assets approaching EOL in the next 6 months.
See image.
To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select Click to View Items to view details of the individual assets for the selected OS.
See image.
OS EOS - Breakdown by Asset OS - Top 10
This chart lists the top 10 operating systems with the highest number of assets affected by EOS. It helps track OS assets using two metrics:

Active Assets in EOS: The dark blue bar represents the current count of assets running on an OS unsupported by its vendor. This indicates a high risk as these assets no longer receive security patches or technical support.

Active Assets with OS EOS in 6 Months: The light blue bar represents the number of assets running operating systems whose support period is scheduled to expire within the next 6 months. This acts as an early warning signal, allowing you to identify potential vulnerabilities before they become active threats.
See image.
To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select Click to View to see the details of the individual assets for the selected OS.
See image.
OS EOL - Breakdown by Asset Owner - Top 5

This chart shows the top 5 owners (e.g., EUC team, Enterprise API team) of assets that are currently at EOL and nearing their EOL date within the next 6 months. It helps track asset ownership using two metrics:
Total Active Assets with OS EOL Upcoming in the Next 6 Months: The dark blue bars represent active assets that will become unsupported within the next 6 months.
Active Assets in EOL: The light blue bars represent active assets already past their EOL date.
See image.
To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select Click to View Items to view details of the individual assets for the selected asset owner.
See image.
OS EOS - Breakdown by Asset Owner - Top 5

This chart shows the top 5 owners of assets that are currently unsupported and nearing their EOS date within the next 6 months (e.g., EUC team, Enterprise API team). It helps track asset ownership using two metrics:
Active Assets in EOS: The dark blue bars represent active assets already past their EOS date.
Total Active Assets with OS EOS Upcoming in the Next 6 Months: The light blue bars represent active assets that will become unsupported within the next 6 months.
This ensures that ownership of remediation is clearly defined and actionable.
See image.
To investigate further, click any bar in the chart and select Click to View Items to view details of the individual assets for the selected asset owner.
See image.
OS EOL - Breakdown by Asset Type

View OS assets that are currently at EOL and nearing their EOL date within the next 6 months by asset type (e.g., Windows workstation, Linux). This enables targeted risk prioritization, allows for tailored remediation strategies, and facilitates accurate budget allocation.
See image.
To investigate further, click the corresponding asset number in the Active Assets in EOL column to see details of individual assets for the selected asset type.
See image.
OS EOS - Breakdown by Asset Type

View OS assets that are currently unsupported and nearing their EOS date within the next 6 months by asset type (e.g., Windows workstation, Linux). This helps teams prioritize immediate security risks, refine IT migration plans, allocate budget, and simplify compliance requirements.
See image.
To investigate further, click the corresponding asset number in the Active Assets in EOS column to see details of individual assets for the selected asset type.
See image.
